findings.summary: A legacy page can still go unaccounted. unreadableFrontmatter only accepts a page whose first line is exactly `---` after dropping a trailing `\r`. A page that starts with a UTF-8 BOM, a blank line, or leading spaces, and has CRLF endings or no closing `---`, fails both readers. It is then not listed in Legacy, Refused or NoProject, and the run can exit 0 with no mention of it.
evidence: legacyPagesOf calls frontmatterBlock first. frontmatterBlock (address.go:81-88) needs a literal `---\n` and returns false for CRLF pages or pages with no closing line.
unreadableFrontmatter then returns ("", false) whenever TrimSuffix(lines[0], "\r") != "---". A BOM before `---` makes that true, and the page is silently skipped (migrate_cards.go:248-250).
Tests cover only pages that start with `---` (migrate_cards_unreadable_test.go:18-23). None has a BOM, a leading blank line or leading whitespace, so this gap is untested.
This is the 'never skipped' guarantee the commit adds for unreadable pages. It holds for pages starting with `---` but not for these starts.
I did not read L66 or the S6 (c) text. The spec file at the target commit has no D-a or D-b match, so I could not check whether a BOM start is out of scope.

findings.summary: The no-project note is printed only after the `if err != nil { return a.refuse(...) }` early return. A run that fails with an internal error, for example a write or backup failure during --apply, never prints the note about the no-project legacy pages. The commit says each run prints it once.
evidence: In reportMigration the error return at lines 91-93 comes before the note block at lines 105-112.
The tests for the note (migrate_card_pages_scan_test.go:11 and :66) only exercise successful runs.
Read migrate_cards.go lines 60-480 and 523-575: refusal kinds, carriesLegacyKeys, unreadableFrontmatter, legacyPagesOf, MigrateCardPages, recordedRewrite, rewrittenIdentity.

Read cmd_migrate_card_pages.go in full: reportMigration, exit codes, refusalReason (lists existing backup dirs), BackUp (removal of a failed copy followed by a directory sync), toleratedDirectorySyncError, syncDirectory.
Read frontmatterBlock and eachPage in address.go.

Read migrate_cards_unreadable_test.go. Grepped the cmd tests: NoProject exit 0 plus the note (scan_test), the unreadable summary line and refused-by-name line (scan_test:51-54), backups present: none or a list (halfmigrated_test), toleratedDirectorySyncError (backup_durable_test).

Exit codes are as the commit describes. Any Refused entry, including RefusedUnreadable, gives exit 6. NoProject entries alone give 0 and print the note on stdout. Unreadable pages are never rewritten. The empty-type and empty-revision recovery candidates are present and tested.

toleratedDirectorySyncError is pure, treats nil as false, and tolerates windows, ErrUnsupported, EINVAL and ENOTSUP. I found no data-safety defect in the failed-copy removal path: the directory is synced after RemoveAll and a sync failure is joined into the error.
